title: Choose the material for the job
caption: Silicon's manufacturing ecosystem and oxide are powerful advantages, while power and optical devices reward different properties. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Silicon logic
nodes.detail: A useful oxide and mature processes support dense switching.

nodes.label: Wide-bandgap power
nodes.detail: SiC and GaN address demanding voltage or switching conditions.

nodes.label: Compound-semiconductor optics
nodes.detail: Direct-bandgap materials enable efficient light emission.

source.heading: Why silicon wins, and where it loses

title: SiGe stressors strain nearby silicon
caption: Embedded SiGe source and drain regions can stress the neighboring silicon channel. These arrows show a mechanical influence, not a vertical layer stack. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: SiGe source region
nodes.detail: Its preferred lattice spacing differs from surrounding silicon.

nodes.label: SiGe drain region
nodes.detail: The other embedded region also contributes mechanical stress.

nodes.label: Silicon channel
nodes.detail: The nearby constrained channel experiences strain that affects carrier transport.

source.heading: Silicon-germanium: the alloy inside every modern transistor

title: Grow thin silicon on a larger lattice
caption: The original strained-silicon approach places a thin Si layer over relaxed SiGe; the overlayer stretches to fit the template. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Thin silicon layer
nodes.detail: The layer is held under tensile strain.

nodes.label: Relaxed SiGe buffer
nodes.detail: A larger lattice spacing acts as the template.

nodes.label: Silicon substrate
nodes.detail: The original wafer supports the engineered buffer.

source.heading: Strained silicon: the idea that went the other way

title: Grow SiC through vapor transport
caption: SiC growth avoids ordinary melt pulling: hot source material supplies vapor that recrystallizes on a cooler seed. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: SiC source
nodes.detail: Heated source material supplies vapor species.

nodes.label: Thermal gradient
nodes.detail: Temperature differences drive transport through the chamber.

nodes.label: Seed crystal
nodes.detail: Vapor deposits onto the growth surface.

nodes.label: SiC boule
nodes.detail: The resulting crystal is sliced for power-device substrates.

source.heading: Silicon carbide: the material you cannot melt

title: The useful channel sits at a heterointerface
caption: An electron channel forms near the AlGaN/GaN interface; it is not a separate bulk material layer. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: AlGaN barrier
nodes.detail: The upper material contributes interface polarization.

nodes.label: GaN layer
nodes.detail: The conducting electron channel forms near the interface with the barrier.

title: Different III–V materials serve different signals
caption: GaAs and InP retain important roles where fast carriers or light emission matter; they do not simply replace silicon CMOS. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: GaAs radio-frequency devices
nodes.detail: Fast electronic behavior supports selected RF functions.

nodes.label: InP optical devices
nodes.detail: Material properties suit important optical communication functions.

nodes.label: Silicon CMOS
nodes.detail: Complementary device integration remains a separate strength.

source.heading: Gallium arsenide and indium phosphide: the III-V workhorses

title: Germanium returns in specialized roles
caption: Germanium's oxide and thermal limitations constrain broad replacement of silicon, but its alloy and optical roles remain useful. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: SiGe alloy partner
nodes.detail: Ge changes lattice spacing and electronic properties.

nodes.label: Optical applications
nodes.detail: Selected devices exploit germanium's optical response.

nodes.label: Specialty substrates
nodes.detail: Niche structures use germanium wafers.

nodes.label: Material selection
nodes.detail: The useful property must outweigh integration constraints.

title: Separate production devices from research options
caption: Today's silicon-based structures provide the reference point; alternative channel materials still require device and manufacturing integration. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Silicon nanosheets
nodes.detail: The established manufacturing direction defines the baseline.

nodes.label: Candidate channel materials
nodes.detail: Research explores new electronic structures.

nodes.label: Integration evidence
nodes.detail: Contacts, defects and reproducibility must be demonstrated.

nodes.label: Manufacturable process
nodes.detail: A promising material must work across a production flow.

source.heading: The periodic table at 2 nm and below

title: The fab depends on several material streams
caption: Substrate, process consumables and packaging materials enter different stages; their importance is not proportional only to mass. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Silicon wafers
nodes.detail: Provide the circuit-building surface.

nodes.label: Fab chemicals and gases
nodes.detail: Repeated unit processes consume specialized inputs.

nodes.label: Packaging materials
nodes.detail: Assembly needs substrates, compounds and connections.

nodes.label: Completed product
nodes.detail: Qualified material streams combine throughout production.

title: A temporary film carries the image
caption: Photoresist changes chemical behavior when exposed, allowing development to leave a spatial pattern. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Coat and bake
nodes.detail: Create a uniform photosensitive film.

nodes.label: Expose
nodes.detail: Light modifies selected regions according to the image.

nodes.label: Develop
nodes.detail: Chemistry removes the soluble regions.

nodes.label: Resist pattern
nodes.detail: The remaining film masks the next process.

title: Gas purity must survive the delivery path
caption: A qualified cylinder is only the beginning: delivery surfaces, purification and flow control also determine what reaches the wafer. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Source gas
nodes.detail: The supplied chemical must meet impurity limits.

nodes.label: Purification and delivery
nodes.detail: Lines and filters preserve the clean gas stream.

nodes.label: Flow control
nodes.detail: The tool meters gases into the recipe.

nodes.label: Process chamber
nodes.detail: Surface reactions depend on the delivered chemistry.

title: Cleaning chemistry must not become contamination
caption: A wet process removes material from the wafer but can also redeposit contaminants unless the chemical and rinse streams are controlled. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Qualified chemical
nodes.detail: High-purity reagent enters the process.

nodes.label: Surface reaction
nodes.detail: The bath dissolves or releases target contamination.

nodes.label: Clean rinse
nodes.detail: UPW carries away reaction products and chemicals.

nodes.label: Contamination control
nodes.detail: Monitoring verifies that cleaning did not add new impurities.

title: Water purification removes several impurity classes
caption: Ionic, organic, particulate and microbial control require complementary treatment stages; resistivity alone does not measure every contaminant. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Bulk purification
nodes.detail: Remove major dissolved and suspended loads.

nodes.label: Fine polishing
nodes.detail: Control residual ions, organics and gases.

nodes.label: Distribution loop
nodes.detail: Keep the treated water clean during circulation.

nodes.label: Point of use
nodes.detail: Final delivery supplies the process rinse.

title: Chemistry and contact work together in CMP
caption: Slurry changes the surface while abrasive particles and pad contact remove it; the coupled process smooths topography. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Reactive slurry
nodes.detail: Chemistry modifies the exposed material.

nodes.label: Reacted surface
nodes.detail: A removable layer forms preferentially under process conditions.

nodes.label: Pad and abrasive
nodes.detail: Contact shears or removes the softened material.

nodes.label: Flatter surface
nodes.detail: Removal reduces protruding topography before the next layer.

returnLabel: Continue surface reaction and removal until the polishing endpoint

title: Move atoms from a solid target to the wafer
caption: Argon ions strike the target; ejected target atoms travel to the substrate and form a film. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Argon plasma
nodes.detail: Ions are produced in the chamber.

nodes.label: Sputter target
nodes.detail: Ion impact knocks atoms out of the solid.

nodes.label: Traveling atoms
nodes.detail: Ejected species cross the low-pressure space.

nodes.label: Deposited film
nodes.detail: Atoms accumulate on the wafer surface.

title: A precursor must be deliverable and reactive
caption: The useful molecule must reach the chamber without decomposing prematurely, then react under the wafer process conditions. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Source container
nodes.detail: A stable precursor is stored under controlled conditions.

nodes.label: Vapor delivery
nodes.detail: Temperature and plumbing support reliable transport.

nodes.label: Reaction region
nodes.detail: Surface chemistry creates the intended film.

nodes.label: Exhaust removal
nodes.detail: Volatile by-products leave the chamber.

title: Hot-zone consumables shape contamination risk
caption: Quartz, silicon and SiC parts face heat and reactive chemistry; erosion and replacement are part of process control. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Quartzware
nodes.detail: Tubes and boats support selected furnace processes.

nodes.label: Silicon parts
nodes.detail: Rings and other parts face process environments.

nodes.label: SiC parts
nodes.detail: Thermally demanding roles use specialized materials.

nodes.label: Stable process chamber
nodes.detail: Part condition influences contamination and repeatability.

title: A reticle has its own precision manufacturing chain
caption: A defect in the master can repeat across many dies, so blank preparation, writing and inspection all matter. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Qualified mask blank
nodes.detail: The substrate and coating establish the starting quality.

nodes.label: Pattern writing
nodes.detail: A mask writer defines the master geometry.

nodes.label: Pattern transfer
nodes.detail: Processing turns the written image into the mask structure.

nodes.label: Inspection and repair
nodes.detail: Qualification finds and corrects printable defects.

source.heading: Photomasks: the supply chain in depth

title: Qualification reinforces specialist materials supply
caption: Materials know-how accumulates through repeated customer feedback and process qualification; replacing a qualified input can require extensive evidence. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Specialist formulation
nodes.detail: Suppliers optimize purity and process behavior.

nodes.label: Customer process
nodes.detail: The material must perform in a specific manufacturing flow.

nodes.label: Qualification and feedback
nodes.detail: Yield and defect results inform acceptance.

nodes.label: Process learning
nodes.detail: Repeated improvements deepen application knowledge.

returnLabel: Process feedback informs the next qualified formulation
